churn_resistance.rationale: Data access, URL construction and configuration are cleanly isolated so a framework upgrade would touch few files, but two real risks remain: every route depends on an undocumented engine internal for build-time detection, and the app is entirely TypeScript with no type checking configured, so type drift across those boundaries will never be caught.

findings.issue: Build-render detection keys off the undocumented 'gracile-static' stub hostname, an engine internal; if a Gracile release changes it, handlers would silently fetch and embed API data at build time instead of failing loudly.
findings.suggestion: Keep the check centralized (it is), but add a second signal or a runtime assertion (e.g. error if a request-time URL ever carries that origin), and raise the convention upstream so it gets a documented API.

findings.issue: No tsconfig.json, no typescript/@types/node devDependencies and no check script, despite 17 TypeScript source files; the official minimal-server-hono starter ships a tsconfig and 'check': 'tsc'. Types are decorative and never verified.
findings.suggestion: Add the starter's tsconfig.json plus typescript/@types/node as devDependencies and a 'check': 'tsc' script wired into the build.

findings.issue: Inline onerror="this.style.visibility='hidden'" attribute on card sprites is incompatible with strict Content-Security-Policy (no-unsafe-inline), which a reverse-proxy production setup is likely to add.
findings.suggestion: Move it into the existing pokemon-filters/pokemon-card custom element script, or use CSS (e.g. aspect-ratio placeholder) to handle missing sprites.

findings.issue: Client enhancers hard-code the server template's element IDs ('results', 'moves-tables'), coupling server templates and client scripts across files.
findings.suggestion: Define the IDs in one shared module (or derive them from the wrapper custom element) so template refactors can't desync the pairs.

findings.issue: TTL cache is process-local with no way to invalidate or observe staleness beyond the 60s window; acceptable for the spec, but a future requirement (e.g. immediate consistency) would require editing the core client.
findings.suggestion: Fine as is; if requirements move, expose a small invalidate() hook rather than letting routes fetch around the cache.

summary: This app is on the current generation of Gracile (0.11.0 stable) and mirrors the framework's official Hono starter almost exactly, from the hono adapter and vite plugin config down to the dependency set, with all versions on latest stable majors. Platform usage is exemplary — fetch/AbortController/DOMParser, native custom elements and modern CSS — with zero extra dependencies. The two things that will age poorly are the reliance on an undocumented engine internal to detect build-time rendering, and the absence of any TypeScript configuration despite an all-TS codebase.
